gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not have heard the announcement — he had headphones on the whole flight.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have heard' — 'can' supplies the negative deduction before 'not have heard'.

gaps.sentence: I have no idea where he is — he ___ have gone to the gym, or maybe to the pool.
gaps.hint: an uncertain guess about the past
gaps.explanation: 'Might have' expresses an uncertain guess about the past: might have gone.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost — there is no such thing!
gaps.hint: a past claim rejected as impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' rejects a past claim as impossible: can't have seen.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on and I can hear the vacuum cleaner, so someone ___ be at home.
gaps.explanation: Evidence-based certainty uses 'must': must be at home.

gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.

gaps.sentence: You ___ worry — I have already sent the invitations.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' reassures someone that an action is unnecessary: needn't worry.
